pr_title: Remove from_state from alarm device triggers

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Remove from_state from alarm_control_panel device triggers

The alarm_control_panel device triggers are broken, the intention is to allow `from_state` to be either `arming` or `pending`, but this evaluates to `pending`: `from_state = STATE_ALARM_PENDING or STATE_ALARM_ARMING`, not a list of strings.

There doesn't seem to be any reason to require the state transitions in the first place, since it's not enforced in any way.

pr_comments:
@springstan Do you remember why you added requirements for state transitions in the first place in #29068?
@MartinHjelmare It would be appreciated if you had a look at this.

The stated reason for the "from_trigger" in #29068 is:

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/29068#discussion_r352320929
"from state is important because else it will trigger if it goes from armed_night -> armed_night when an attribute changes."

But if that's really  case it seems like a better approach is to protect from all triggers if the state itself has not changed from previous state rather than try to condition all of the possible from-to pairs that could potentially occur.  At least that's my very non-expert opinion.

@tsightler yes, I was just about to write something similar; we want to set up a trigger that fires on a state change.
I'll mark this as draft since it's not the correct solution.

Edit: I think @ballob's comment was not correct. If there is a defined `from_state` or `to_state`, the state trigger doesn't fire on attribute changes. We only fire on attribute changes if *both* to_state and from_state are left empty or explicitly set to `*`:
```py
        # When we listen for state changes with `match_all`, we
        # will trigger even if just an attribute changes. When
        # we listen to just an attribute, we should ignore all
        # other attribute changes.
        if attribute is not None and old_value == new_value:
            return

        if (
            not match_from_state(old_value)
            or not match_to_state(new_value)
            or (not match_all and old_value == new_value) # This will not accept only attribute changes
        ):
            return
```

Something similar (but not broken) is done in other device triggers, for example in vacuum device trigger:
```py
    if config[CONF_TYPE] == "cleaning":
        from_state = [state for state in STATES if state != STATE_CLEANING]
        to_state = STATE_CLEANING
    else:
        from_state = [state for state in STATES if state != STATE_DOCKED]
        to_state = STATE_DOCKED
```

Still, I don't think it's necessary and should be simplified?

issue_context.title: Some device triggered automations don't work with MQTT Alarm Control Panel
issue_context.body:
## The problem
I maintain a simple addon that allows the Ring alarm system to interface with Home Assistant via MQTT that is moderately popular.  The solution seems to work well for most people but, over the last few months, I've had multiple users report that attempting to leverage a device level automation works for cases when the alarm enters "disarmed" state, but not when the alarm enters "armed_home" or "armed_away" state.

I've tried to troubleshoot this myself, but indeed, I've become stumped, it simply seems that states other than "disarmed" do not create any device level triggers.  As all I can do is send the states supported by the MQTT Alarm Control Panel components, I assume this problem cannot be on my side and must be some issue with the component itself.

The workaround is to simply build a "state" based trigger for the entity, which works perfectly, but it seems like this should not be required, especially since device level automation does work for "disarmed" state.  I tried to follow the code for device triggers for the alarm control panel, but not being very skilled at Python made this a little difficult.

## Environment

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue:  2021.1.0
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): Docker but reported by users on different platforms
- Integration causing this issue: MQTT Alarm Control Panel
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/alarm_control_panel.mqtt/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
Here's an example YAML for a device trigger based automation that doesn't work:

platform: device
device_id: XXX
domain: alarm_control_panel
entity_id: alarm_control_panel.ring_alarm
type: armed_home

On the other hand this will work:

trigger:
  - platform: state
    entity_id: alarm_control_panel.ring_alarm
    to: armed_home
comments:
An `armed_home` device trigger is only generated if the entity has set `SUPPORT_ALARM_ARM_HOME`.

Also, the relevant code in HA translates device trigger `armed_home` to this state trigger:
```py
    if config[CONF_TYPE] == "armed_home":
        from_state = STATE_ALARM_PENDING or STATE_ALARM_ARMING
        to_state = STATE_ALARM_ARMED_HOME
```

Does the Ring alarm system entities meet these requirements?
Maybe you can share an MQTT discovery message for setting up a corresponding mqtt.alarm_control_panel?

Also, I'm not sure if the assumption that `from_state` must be ` STATE_ALARM_PENDING` or `STATE_ALARM_ARMING` is always correct.
This was added in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/32950

@MartinHjelmare: transitioning through ` STATE_ALARM_PENDING` or `STATE_ALARM_ARMING` doesn't seem to be enforced by the base component, how can we guarantee that's always the case, and why does the device trigger require that transition?

Hi, thanks for the response.

I believe that the Ring alarm component meets the requirements.  The attribute supported_features = 23, which, if I'm understanding how this attribute works, indicates that `SUPPORT_ALARM_ARM_HOME` is set, and I'm pretty sure that's the default for the MQTT alarm control panel component (I don't think you can NOT have this).

Here's a slightly redacted discovery packet:

```
name: Ring Alarm
unique_id: f116795a-c2xx-4cxx-8exx-d19fxxxxxxxx
availability_topic: >-
  ring/a9ce28cb-faxx-42xx-45xx-29d54xxxxxxx/alarm/f116795a-c2xx-4cxx-8exx-d19fxxxxxxxx/status
payload_available: online
payload_not_available: offline
state_topic: >-
  ring/a9ce28cb-faxx-42xx-45xx-29d54xxxxxxx/alarm/f116795a-c2xx-4cxx-8exx-d19fxxxxxxxx/alarm/state
command_topic: >-
  ring/a9ce28cb-faxx-42xx-45xx-29d54xxxxxxx/alarm/f116795a-c2xx-4cxx-8exx-d19fxxxxxxxx/alarm/command
device:
  identifiers:
    - f116795a-c2xx-4cxx-8exx-d19fxxxxxxxx
  name: Ring Alarm
  manufacturer: Ring
  model: Alarm Control Panel
platform: mqtt
```

I saw in the code the conditions around requiring "arming" state before going to "armed_home" or "armed_away", and ring-mqtt does not currently implement this state, it goes straight from disarmed to "armed_home" or "armed_away" and I saw some of this described in the logic of the state machine for the manual alarm, so that was somewhat of a guess.

However, I tried to get the device triggers to work by manually sending the states via MQTT.  If I sent "arming" the UI would reflect the state change and the alarm control panel card would show the "arming" state, but even then if I sent "armed_home" or "armed_away" command not device trigger automation occurred.  The only one that consistently works in "disarmed".

This made me think that the problem has to be in the MQTT alarm control panel component and so I opened this issue looking for guidance as I can't see that ring-mqtt is doing anything wrong here, it's just sending state after all and that is properly reflected in the entity and "disarmed" trigger works.

The base component is broken; the intention in #32950 was to allow `from_state` to be either `arming` or `pending`, but this evaluates to `pending`:  `from_state = STATE_ALARM_PENDING or STATE_ALARM_ARMING`
I don't see any reason why the alarm_control_panel device triggers should depend on a `from_state`, I'll open a PR to remove that.

review_comments: We had a from_state (although this is obviously wrong) because otherwise if an attribute updates, the state remains the same and it shouldn't trigger.
I don't think that's the case: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/homeassistant/triggers/state.py#L109-L121
We only trigger on attributes if *both* `from_state` and `to_state` are set to `*` (or not specified)
You are right and I am wrong.
